title: Data Structures & Algorithms
courseObjectives: To introduce foundational concepts of abstract data types and algorithmic complexity.
To analyze linear and non-linear data structures including trees, balanced search structures, and graphs.
To design and evaluate efficient sorting, searching, and hashing strategies for computational tasks.

clos.statement: Analyze the asymptotic time and space complexity of iterative and recursive algorithms using Big-O, Big-Omega, and Big-Theta notations.
Construct and implement singly linked, doubly linked, circular linked lists, stacks, and circular queues for dynamic memory management.
Evaluate binary trees, binary search trees (BST), and AVL tree self-balancing rotations during dynamic data updates.
Design graph models and compute shortest paths, topological sort orders, and minimum spanning trees using BFS, DFS, Dijkstra, and Kruskal algorithms.
Implement collision resolution strategies in hash tables including separate chaining and open addressing with linear and quadratic probing.

units.title: Linear Data Structures & Algorithm Complexity
units.content: Asymptotic notation, amortized analysis, Singly & Doubly Linked Lists, Array-based stacks and queues.

units.title: Tree Hierarchies & Balanced Search Structures
units.content: Binary Trees, BST operations, AVL Trees, balancing rotations, B-Trees & Red-Black tree principles.

units.title: Graph Theory & Network Traversal
units.content: Graph representations, BFS, DFS, topological sorting, Dijkstra shortest path, Kruskal and Prim MST.

units.title: Hashing & Priority Queues
units.content: Hash functions, collision resolution, binary heaps, priority queue operations, heap sort.

units.title: Sorting Paradigms & Advanced Applications
units.content: Divide and conquer, QuickSort, MergeSort, RadixSort, Disjoint-Set Data Structures (Union-Find).
